allow.why: REFUSED, AND IT IS A HARD CSS FACT RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. .d-slider__input::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb are six declarations against six at 100% - the same thumb, twice, because there is no other way to write it. A selector list containing a pseudo-element the browser does not recognise is INVALID AS A WHOLE: Chromium drops the entire rule when it meets ::-moz-range-thumb, and Firefox drops it when it meets ::-webkit-slider-thumb. Merging them would leave the slider thumb unstyled in every browser at once - the one merge in this report that would break the thing it tidied. The values are single-sourced through the tokens either way, which is the part that has to hold.

allow.why: REFUSED, AND THIS IS THE DECISION THE PLAN ASKED FOR. The merge plan listed "the ratio box" as a batch 4 item: .d-frame and .d-skeleton share position:relative, display:block, overflow:hidden and border-radius:var(--radius-s). That is the generic "a block that clips its contents", not an object. .d-frame is the box a PICTURE sits in and carries --ratio and aspect-ratio, which a skeleton must never inherit; a skeleton is a placeholder that shimmers and is grey. Merging them would mean the next change to how photographs are clipped arrives inside the loading state. The honest version of this is markup, not CSS - a skeleton that stands in for a frame should BE a .d-frame with a skeleton modifier, and then the shared four come for free. Two members and no third is also exactly the case the triage refused for .d-cluster: it fixes 2 of 2 and names no object.

allow.why: COINCIDENCE, RE-RECORDED BECAUSE THE OTHER SIDE OF THE PAIR CHANGED. .woocommerce table.shop_attributes th is a ROW LABEL - the left column of a spec sheet - not a column header. It shares text-align:left, the quiet ink, border:0 and the hairline under it with the real header cell, and differs on both things that decide what a cell IS: fs-meta/lh-body against fs-fine/lh-title, and an asymmetric padding because the label hangs off the left edge of the table.

COINCIDENCE, AND IT ONLY EXISTS BECAUSE THE PAGINATOR CELL GOT SHORTER. A notice's dismiss button and a paginator number now share exactly four declarations - position:relative, z-index:2, cursor:pointer and a colour transition - which is "a small control that lifts above its neighbour and fades its ink", a shape rather than an object. One closes a message and one goes to page four. Worth noting separately: .d-notice__dismiss carries the icon-button signature (appearance:none, border:0, background:none, padding:0, cursor:pointer) without being on the .d-icon-btn family list, but it draws its cross with a FONT rather than a mask and is radius-xs rather than a circle, so joining that family is a component change and not a merge.

REAL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED AT THE END OF A BATCH. .d-progress__native and .d-slider__input are one object - a native form control with the browser's chrome taken off, filling its column: appearance:none twice, display:block, width:100%. The pair appeared only because this commit shortened the progress rule, which is how it should surface. It is not merged because there is no honest home for it yet: the two live in different pattern files, so putting the base in either one couples a slider to a progress bar, and the right answer is a base-layer rule for "a native control we draw ourselves" that does not exist. Inventing a file in the last five minutes of a batch is how a system gains one nobody remembers. Candidate for the same pass as patterns/wake.css in batch 6.

REAL, AND THE HONEST RESIDUE OF THE MERGE THAT JUST HAPPENED. The paginator's trail and the slider's are now one rule in patterns/wake.css - twenty-one lines of paint that used to be written twice. .d-wipe::after is the same idea at a third of the size and is painted DIFFERENTLY on purpose: three sparks rather than six and a shorter fade, because it is .55rem tall and six sparks in that box is a smudge. It shares the shape - absolutely positioned, centred on its line, pill-ended, untouchable, starting invisible - and sharing THAT was tried in the first version of wake.css: a five-declaration shape rule immediately scored against a panel's edge wash, an icon button's hover glow and the scrollbar's trail, and the pair count went UP by three. Shape is not an object. Note the count did not move for this one either: collapsing two copies into one rule leaves that one rule still resembling a third thing. The duplication went; the pair did not.

COINCIDENCE, and the triage already refused its sibling. A cart row and a notice share position:relative, display:grid, align-items:start, a gap and a meta size. The drawer line is a four-track row built around a 3.25rem photograph; the notice is a two-track message with a surface. The same reasoning that kept .d-drawer__head out of .d-drawer__line__foot applies: the next change to the cart row must not arrive inside every notice on the site.

allow.why: CROSS-ORIGIN, AND IT IS THE SAME BOX ON A DIFFERENT KIND OF ELEMENT. .wc-blocks-components-select__container is a WRAPPER: WooCommerce draws its custom select as a div around a real <select>, and the div is what carries the hairline, the radius, the raised fill and the focus transition - four declarations it shares with the field box because it IS the field box. It cannot join .d-field__control's list, which also hands out width:100%, a min-height, padding, body type, ink and appearance:none - all of which belong to the CONTROL inside the wrapper, not to the wrapper. Folding it in would pad the box twice and set a height on something whose height is its child. The honest version is a named "field box" that both the control and this wrapper wear, which is a bigger change than a merge: it means splitting .d-field__control into a box half and a control half, the way .d-icon was split into geometry and mask plumbing. Worth doing; not worth doing at the end of a batch.
